transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, doctor. Well, I came in today because... I guess I just keep steering clear of my own workshop lately. That, and I've been avoiding any family get-togethers if there's a chance my brother-in-law might show up. 

It's been going on a while, and honestly, after all this time I'm just getting really tired of having to plan my whole life around not running into those reminders.
Do unwanted memories or nightmares about what happened come back to you repeatedly?

Yeah, they do. Sometimes, just completely out of nowhere, I'll see his hand with that heavy tool again. It's... well, it's like a picture that just pops right into my head. I could be doing something completely ordinary, like shaving in the morning or working on a painting, and suddenly it's just there. And honestly, it still makes my chest tighten up every time it happens.
How long have these unwanted memories and avoidance been happening?
Well, it's been going on since that confrontation I had with my brother-in-law. That was... let's see, about two years and four months ago now. So, yeah, it's been happening ever since then.
Since the confrontation, have you often felt constantly on guard or watchful for danger?

Yes, I do. It's... well, even when I'm just down at the senior center, or at a gathering in the church basement, I find myself always checking to see who just came in. I make sure I know exactly where the door is, and... I just really don't like it if I don't know whether anyone is standing too close behind me. I guess I just always feel the need to keep an eye on things now.
During the confrontation, did you believe that you might be seriously injured or killed?

Well, to be honest, I'm not really sure. I mean... I saw the tool, and I knew he was furious, but I don't know if I actually thought I was going to be killed or anything like that. It all happened pretty fast. I guess I didn't really have time to think about how bad it could get... I just knew it was a bad situation and I needed to get away from him.
During the confrontation, did your brother-in-law actually strike you or use the tool in a way that threatened to cause you serious physical injury?
No, he didn't actually hit me. He was just yelling and waving it around, acting crazy. He didn't swing it at me or anything like that.
During the confrontation, did your brother-in-law explicitly threaten to seriously hurt or kill you?

No, he didn't say anything like that. I mean, he was cussing and hollering a lot, just really out of his mind with anger, but... he never actually said the words that he was going to kill me or put me in the hospital. It was mostly just yelling about the argument we were having, not a direct threat like that.
